text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** NMC's main advantage is lighter cells, and in finished power stations that edge is often small.

## Head-to-head

| | LiFePO4 (LFP) | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle life** | Typically 3,000–6,000 rated cycles | Typically 500–1,000 (some up to ~2,000) |
| **Failure behavior** | Burns cooler and slower | Hotter, more violent thermal runaway |
| **Weight** | Heavier cells | Lighter cells, but the gap shrinks in a full unit |
| **Price** | Now mainstream and often cheaper per Wh | Mostly legacy, clearance or ultra-compact models |
| **Cold charging** | Most won't charge below 32°F | Same |

## Key points

**1. Cycle life is the real difference.** OutageMath's database of 54 models shows a median rating of 4,000 cycles for LFP and 800 for NMC. With daily solar cycling, an 800-cycle unit reaches its rated limit in about 2.2 years, versus about 11 years for 4,000 cycles. [outagemath.com](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)

Check the fine print: "4,000 to 70%" is a weaker promise than "4,000 to 80%."

**2. Safety favors LFP, though it isn't fireproof.** In lab tests, an NMC cell peaked at 731°C while an LFP cell peaked at 259°C. [outagemath.com](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)

However, in a 2020 overcharge study, the LFP cell went into thermal runaway *earlier*. When it failed, it smoked without flames, while the NMC cells ignited. [unpluggedwatts.com](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)

Be skeptical of claims that LFP is "virtually impossible to catch fire." A good battery management system matters for both chemistries.

**3. The weight advantage is smaller than expected.** NMC cells are much denser. But the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. In same-brand pairs like the Jackery Explorer 1000 and the 1000 v2, LFP is only slightly heavier per kWh while offering several times the cycle rating. [outagemath.com](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)

**4. Cost now favors LFP too.** One site's listings show a median price of $0.55 per Wh for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC. [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)

## When NMC still makes sense
- You need the lightest possible unit and will use it only a few times a year.
- You find a deeply discounted clearance unit for light use.
- You already own a working NMC station. There's no reason to replace it.

For an outage kit used a few times a year, either chemistry works. Aging over time and proper storage will matter more than cycle count.
